newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Khatami submits cabinet to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Khatami submits cabinet to parliament.

text.p: Iran's President Mohammad Khatami on Tuesday submitted his choice of cabinet ministers to parliament for approval, naming a new foreign minister and a new oil minister.

A letter containing the names of Khatami's proposed 22-member cabinet had been received by parliament, Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri said in a live broadcast carried by Tehran radio from the assembly.
Parliament must endorse the proposed cabinet in three five-hour sessions.

Khatami, elected Iran's fifth president on May 23 and seen as a moderate, nominated outgoing energy minister Bijan Namdar Zanganeh as oil minister and Iran's ambassador to the United Nations Kamal Kharrazi as foreign minister.

If approved by parliament, Kharrazi, in his 50s, would replace Ali Akbar Velayati, who has been foreign minister since two years after the 1979 Islamic revolution. Kharrazi has been Iran's ambassador to the world body since 1990.

Zanganeh, if approved, would replace veteran oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh, who is expected to retain an important position in a mediating council headed by outgoing president Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
As energy minister Zanganeh oversaw Iran's domestic power sector and its non-petroleum related energy sector.
Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter behind Saudi Arabia and Norway and is the second largest producer in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).

Khatami's letter to parliament listed navy chief Rear-Admiral Ali Shamkhani as defence minister. Shamkhani in recent years has been in charge of the overhaul of the navy and deployment of Russian submarines and Chinese missiles and warships.
Hossein Namazi had been chosen for the economy and finance post.
Five of the 22 ministers proposed were carried over from Rafsanjani's administration, including Issa Kalantari at agriculture and Hossein Kamali at labour and social affairs.
